topic: Solve minimax annealed causal assignment with known target-population cell masses and capacity, lambda_n=kappa/sqrt(n), and a fixed-dimensional Gaussian contact experiment. Characterize the scalar reverse-KL minimax rule, its least-favorable prior, strict plug-in risk gap, certified computation, and temperature limits. Then solve the weighted multivariate capacity problem by recursive exposed-face Gaussian experiments, proving compatible minimax maps, polynomial certified risk/map approximation, and strict separation from coordinatewise linear-logit shrinkers. Finally derive the observed-data causal LAN lower bound and an exactly capacity-feasible cross-fitted learner with estimated covariance, expanding-local attainment, and honest policy/welfare confidence sets. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent presolve derived the scalar posterior-Bayes identity delta(z)=expit(E[H|Z=z]/kappa), nonrandomized minimax existence, essential uniqueness, symmetry, monotonicity, strict shrinkage, and a proper least-favorable prior whose support must be locally finite, countably infinite, and unbounded in both directions. Interval calculations certify that at kappa=1 the plug-in worst risk exceeds that of expit(0.8Z) by more than 0.0141. It also derived projected Gaussian experiments on every exposed capacity face, lower bounds from face risks, and an upper bound forcing risk to vanish with residual capacity. The corrected four-arm Bernoulli path has Fisher information one, and known target masses make exact population capacity feasible. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove compatible minimax extensions across nested exposed faces, essential multivariate uniqueness, polynomial certified value and expected-KL map recovery, strict separation from every common positive scaling, and covariance-stable expanding-local causal attainment. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the three-cell equal-mass, half-capacity problem with contact covariance diag(1,4), certify all six edge extensions, and test normal rays, tangential offsets, and near-wall directions; pivot if face limits are incompatible or the coupled optimum lies in the declared diagonal class. open_problems.open_problem: In the scalar Gaussian contact experiment for capacity-constrained annealed assignment, characterize the exact reverse-KL minimax rule, every proper least-favorable prior, its strict worst-risk advantage over plug-in assignment, and its kappa-to-zero and kappa-to-infinity limits.

source_refs.claim: Capacity makes assignments interdependent; the paper proves average local optimality and leaves capacity-constrained minimax optimality as a differentiability-linked conjecture.
source_refs.author: Keita Sunada and Kohei Izumi

source_refs.claim: Fractional Gaussian Bayes and minimax rules are logistic under nonlinear treatment regret, but aggregate capacity and reverse-KL oracle loss are not treated.
source_refs.author: Toru Kitagawa, Sokbae Lee, and Chen Qiu

source_refs.claim: Gaussian limit experiments yield local asymptotic minimax treatment rules for standard welfare-regret losses.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

source_refs.excerpt: the published construction gives an exact finite-n saddle and a correspondingly lifted least-favorable prior.
specify the finite-support search dimension or a Caratheodory-style support-size target for the dual program.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kitagawa-Lee-Qiu obtain logistic fractional rules for a different nonlinear loss, while Sunada-Izumi establish average rather than minimax optimality under capacity. Prior CausalSmith work imports finite or compact least-favorable-prior arguments, but reverse KL changes the Bayes step to a logistic transform of a posterior mean and leaves a noncompact Gaussian parameter space. The missing proof must establish tight dual attainment, analyze the analytic equalizer equation to determine whether support is locally finite, countably infinite, and unbounded in both tails, and control the rule uniformly as temperature degenerates. Existing slicing arguments do not simultaneously provide uniqueness, support geometry, strict plug-in separation, and both temperature limits.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A saddle-point theorem deriving the posterior-logistic Bayes identity, an essentially unique minimax map, necessary-and-sufficient support conditions for proper least-favorable priors, a certified positive plug-in excess-risk bound, and uniform risk/map convergence in both temperature limits.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from hard treatment choice to an evidence-sensitive fractional Gaussian minimax rule.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hard treatment choice ignores decision uncertainty -> nonlinear loss makes fractional assignment optimal -> reverse-KL annealing poses the capacity-constrained Gaussian minimax problem

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce to a scalar sufficient statistic, derive the fractional posterior-Bayes response, and establish minimaxity through equalizer-risk calculations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest scalar Gaussian logistic minimax argument, with the loss-specific Bayes condition as the step to replace.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct discrete least-favorable priors under KL risk by adding support points that flatten Bayes-risk peaks, and prove strict plug-in suboptimality through risk diversification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result likewise combines Gaussian observations, KL loss, a nontrivial least-favorable prior, and strict plug-in separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer a solved Gaussian-shift minimax problem to causal experiments through convergence of experiments and local asymptotic minimax bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical bridge from the scalar Gaussian solution to a sharp causal local-risk statement.

open_problems.open_problem: For weighted multivariate Gaussian annealed assignment under capacity, determine whether minimax rules on all nested exposed faces admit one compatible global extension, and whether that extension is essentially unique and strictly better than every common positive coordinatewise linear-logit scaling.

source_refs.claim: Fixed treatment masses turn assignment into a coupling with nonpointwise coordination across target-population cells.
source_refs.author: Keita Sunada and Kohei Izumi

source_refs.claim: Entropy-regularized transport has primal-dual optimality conditions and regularized well-posedness, but not a minimax Gaussian map assembled across exposed faces.
source_refs.author: Christian Clason, Dirk A. Lorenz, Hinrich Mahler, and Benedikt Wirth

source_refs.claim: Gaussian treatment-choice problems can admit many minimax-regret rules and require an additional selection principle for uniqueness.

source_refs.excerpt: derive a compatible limiting generator on simplex faces and corners.
Replace pointwise matching by a primal-dual-gap inequality uniform over the set-valued saddle correspondence.
state a concrete generic nonseparability or separability criterion for the K=3 contrast

open_problems.why_unsolved: Transport duality gives a unique interior optimizer for a fixed cost, but facewise minimaxity does not imply that Gaussian Bayes rules derived on different exposed faces agree on their intersections. Prior CausalSmith work independently leaves compatibility at simplex faces and corners unresolved and calls for a concrete three-arm separability criterion. The scalar equalizer argument must be replaced by a face-indexed recursion plus a cocycle or gluing theorem over the weighted-capacity normal fan. Strict convexity alone also cannot exclude every common-scaling coordinatewise logit, because those rules ignore covariance while the required separation is a worst-risk comparison over the entire scaling class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient face-compatibility theorem constructing an essentially unique global minimax map, or a certified three-cell covariance-diag(1,4) counterexample, together with an explicit positive lower bound on the infimum risk gap over all common positive logit scalings.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames capacity as the source of nonpointwise coordination and casts assignment as a coupling problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unconstrained assignments optimize cell by cell -> fixed target masses couple all cell decisions -> multivariate contacts require compatible minimax decisions across exposed faces

method_exemplars.technique: Use Fenchel duality and primal-dual optimality conditions for entropy-regularized couplings, including regularization-limit control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: KKT potentials give natural coordinates for describing the capacity map and its exposed-face limits.

method_exemplars.technique: Solve Gaussian treatment decisions on parameter slices and lift them using decision-theoretic completeness arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every exposed face supplies a projected Gaussian experiment; the new step is compatible lifting across the entire normal fan.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze Gaussian risk sets and apply a secondary extremal criterion to select among multiple minimax randomized rules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its machinery directly addresses possible minimax nonuniqueness at intersections of capacity faces.

open_problems.open_problem: Under an observational causal model with known target-cell masses, determine when an exactly capacity-feasible cross-fitted learner with estimated contact covariance attains the multivariate Gaussian minimax value uniformly over expanding local parameter sets.

source_refs.claim: Local asymptotic minimax treatment rules transfer from Gaussian shifts to regular causal models, but without aggregate capacity or learned face-sensitive covariance.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: Cross-fitted doubly robust scores yield observational policy learners with regret guarantees, but not sharp local minimax attainment for annealed exact-capacity rules.
source_refs.author: Susan Athey and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: The proposed resource-constrained rule estimator is not guaranteed to satisfy population capacity, and constraint-guaranteed estimation is identified as further work.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: When resource use must be estimated, welfare maximization and budget feasibility cannot be attained uniformly over a broad model class, highlighting the role of known target masses.

source_refs.excerpt: Ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN does not imply the experiment-equivalence premise.
Prove a uniform data-only upper theorem using primitive nuisance learnability and local-complexity conditions.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hirano-Porter supplies the LAN template and Athey-Wager supplies orthogonal cross-fitting, but neither handles an estimated-covariance, face-recursive, entropy-annealed map satisfying an exact population capacity equality. Luedtke-van der Laan explicitly lack constraint-guaranteed rule estimation, while known target masses remove the particular impossibility mechanism identified by Sun. Prior CausalSmith reviews also warn that pointwise LAN is insufficient and request a uniform data-only upper theorem. The first failed step is ordinary continuous mapping: face changes make stability of the minimax rule stronger than consistency of the score and covariance estimator, especially on expanding local sets.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A semiparametric convolution or LAN lower-bound theorem and a cross-fitted orthogonal-score construction whose finite-sample map satisfies known population capacity exactly and whose normalized worst risk converges uniformly to the Gaussian minimax value over an explicit expanding sequence of local sets.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames observational policy learning through semiparametric efficiency and application-specific constraints.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational policies require nuisance estimation -> orthogonal cross-fitted scores recover efficient causal information -> known target masses permit exact capacity while Gaussian minimax structure determines local optimality

method_exemplars.technique: Derive Gaussian-shift lower bounds through limits of experiments and prove attainment by matching original-data decisions to Gaussian rules under local alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested theorem is a capacity-constrained, estimated-covariance, expanding-local extension of this transfer.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Neyman-orthogonal scores, cross-fitting, and product-rate remainder bounds to obtain root-n Gaussian approximation with estimated covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The contact vector and covariance must be learned without first-order nuisance bias before applying the Gaussian minimax map.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the resource-constrained value's canonical gradient and express stochastic allocation using a capacity threshold and boundary randomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its resource constraint and stochastic boundary assignment are the closest observed-data objects, while exact feasibility is its explicit missing property.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the fixed-dimensional scalar and multivariate Gaussian reverse-KL capacity games be solved by a certified polynomial-time algorithm that approximates both minimax value and the recovered map in expected reverse KL?

source_refs.claim: Sinkhorn scaling gives near-linear-time additive approximation guarantees for finite optimal transport.
source_refs.author: Jason Altschuler, Jonathan Weed, and Philippe Rigollet

source_refs.claim: Entropic penalization of finite linear programs has explicit nonasymptotic convergence and optimal-face distance bounds.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Weed

source_refs.claim: Regularized transport has explicit approximation and sample-complexity bounds whose conditioning deteriorates with temperature.
source_refs.author: Aude Genevay, Lénaïc Chizat, Francis Bach, Marco Cuturi, and Gabriel Peyré

source_refs.excerpt: certificate uses exact restricted-game and worst-state oracles and deliberately makes no complexity-rate claim.
a rational grid-action hierarchy with a proved approximation bracket

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing transport algorithms certify a finite problem with known costs, whereas this game has a semi-infinite adversarial parameter, Gaussian integration over an unbounded observation space, and conditioning changes near exposed faces and temperature limits. Prior CausalSmith certificates assume exact oracles or omit complexity rates. The missing proof step is a finite reduction with simultaneous discretization, Gaussian-tail, optimization, and dual lower-bound control; then conditional strong convexity of reverse KL must convert value error into expected-KL map error. A Sinkhorn residual or value bracket alone does not certify recovery of the essentially unique minimax map.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For fixed dimension and rational bounded inputs, an algorithm running polynomially in input size and an explicit accuracy parameter that outputs rational upper and lower minimax-value certificates within epsilon and an exactly capacity-feasible map within epsilon expected reverse KL of the minimax rule.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates optimal transport as a computational representation of capacity-constrained treatment assignment.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Capacity-constrained policy choice is coupled -> transport structure makes computation plausible -> Gaussian minimax uncertainty requires certified value and map approximation

method_exemplars.technique: Convert entropic objective gaps into explicit distance-to-optimal-face bounds using polyhedral geometry and exponential-convergence estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The certificate must control approach to lower-dimensional capacity faces as temperature and numerical tolerance vary.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine matrix scaling, marginal-preserving rounding, and explicit primal error accounting to obtain additive transport guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Marginal-preserving rounding is the natural inner solver after finitely reducing the Gaussian adversarial problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use dual-potential regularity to separate entropic approximation error from empirical integration error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired algorithm must separately certify temperature bias, Gaussian integration error, optimization error, and recovered-map error.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest confidence sets for annealed capacity-constrained policy welfare and for an expected-KL neighborhood of the policy map at Gaussian contact points with threshold mass, estimated covariance, and nested-face nonuniqueness.

source_refs.claim: Regular efficient inference for resource-constrained value excludes positive mass at the capacity threshold; no formal theorem is supplied for threshold mass.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: Pathwise differentiability can fail for possibly nonunique optimal treatment strategies, although stabilized online estimation can still yield confidence intervals under stated conditions.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: Softmax smoothing supports root-n inference for irregular optimal-policy values but does not impose exact aggregate capacity or cover face-recursive minimax maps.
source_refs.author: Justin Whitehouse, Morgane Austern, and Vasilis Syrgkanis

open_problems.why_unsolved: Capacity contact is precisely the regime excluded by regular canonical-gradient theory: positive threshold mass makes the constrained optimum nonunique and the value or map only directionally differentiable. Annealing at lambda_n=kappa/sqrt(n) places smoothing bias on the same scale as sampling noise, while nested exposed faces introduce simultaneous contact directions. Existing stabilized-online and softmax methods treat an unconstrained pointwise maximum or a scalar resource threshold, not joint coverage for a covariance-estimated minimax coupling satisfying exact capacity. Standard Wald inference therefore lacks a uniform linear expansion at the regimes requiring coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-set construction proving uniform asymptotic coverage over an explicit contact class for both welfare and an expected-KL neighborhood of the exactly capacity-feasible policy map, together with a nondegenerate local-power or diameter bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates inference for resource-constrained treatment value and isolates threshold mass as the boundary of its regular theory.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Resource limits define a capacity threshold -> regular inference works without threshold mass -> honest inference remains unresolved at threshold and multivariate face contacts

method_exemplars.technique: Use stabilized online one-step estimation and martingale normalization to obtain coverage when optimal rules may be nonunique.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Capacity contacts create the same nonuniqueness mechanism, now coupled across multiple cells and exposed faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Smooth an expected maximum, debias the smoothed functional, and balance smoothing bias against second-order nuisance remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Root-n annealing makes its smoothing-bias accounting directly relevant to inference at capacity contacts.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish Gaussian-process limits for entropic transport potentials and weak limits for associated couplings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Policy-map confidence sets require coupling-level weak convergence in addition to scalar welfare inference.

literature_map:
Manski (2004, Econometrica, 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2004.00530.x) founded finite-sample minimax-regret treatment rules but did not solve annealed capacity coupling.
Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA6630) solved Gaussian-shift treatment decisions and supplied the causal LAN transfer template.
Stoye (2009, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2009.02.013) showed exact minimax rules can materially differ from empirical-success plug-ins.
Bhattacharya and Dupas (2012, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2011.11.007) studied welfare allocation under a binding budget and plug-in welfare inference.
Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, IJB, 10.1515/ijb-2015-0007) characterized resource-constrained stochastic rules but left exact population-feasibility and threshold-mass inference incomplete.
Kitagawa and Tetenov (2018, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA13288) established minimax-optimal welfare convergence rates for empirical welfare maximization.
Athey and Wager (2021, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA15732) combined observational identification, orthogonal scores, and policy regret without sharp capacity-contact minimaxity.
Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye (2023, arXiv:2312.17623) exposed randomization and multiplicity in Gaussian minimax treatment choice.
Kitagawa, Lee, and Qiu (2026, Biometrika, 10.1093/biomet/asag008) derived logistic fractional Gaussian Bayes/minimax rules for mean-square regret, the closest scalar analogue to reverse-KL annealing.
Sunada and Izumi (2025, arXiv:2506.12225) cast fixed-mass assignment as optimal transport and proved average local optimality while leaving minimax optimality open.
Sun (2026, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106169) proved a welfare-feasibility uniformity obstruction when resource use must be estimated, clarifying the value of known target masses.
Clason et al. (2021, JMAA, 10.1016/j.jmaa.2020.124432) and Weed (2018, arXiv:1806.01879) provide entropy duality and explicit optimal-face control, but not adversarial Gaussian-risk certification.
Altschuler, Weed, and Rigollet (2017, arXiv:1705.09634) and Genevay et al. (2019, arXiv:1810.02733) give Sinkhorn guarantees with temperature-sensitive conditioning.
Mukherjee and Johnstone (2015, Annals of Statistics, 10.1214/14-AOS1251) show Gaussian KL prediction can require discrete least-favorable priors and can strictly improve on plug-in rules.
Whitehouse, Austern, and Syrgkanis (2026, arXiv:2507.11780) obtain softmax-based inference for irregular policy values, but exact capacity and nested faces remain outside their framework.
prior_proposal_map:
A catalogue-wide scan covered 399 proposal cores and rejected-angle archives under CausalSmith/doc/research.
The closest source was stat_nonsmooth_asymmetric_mmr_saddle_v2's rejected angle, which yielded active-face stability, a normal-fan indexability question, an interval-certified non-index witness, the absence of a complexity rate, and the warning that pointwise LAN is insufficient.
The accepted exp_multiarm_secondorder_minimax_frontier_v1 core and angle0_v3-v5 reviews supplied the unresolved compatible simplex-face generator, the K=3 separability criterion, a rational certificate hierarchy, and a least-favorable-prior convergence boundary.
The accepted stat_policy_regret_margin_overlap_v1 core and stage_0.5.G review supplied the unresolved uniform data-only cross-fitted upper theorem under primitive nuisance learnability.
The downgraded stat_neyman_regret_minimax_v1 core and angle0_v1-v2 reviews supplied the compact extremal-law dual and the request for finite-support or Carathéodory control.
exp_bipartite_minimax_design_v1 and pid_recurrent_capacity_transport_regret_v1 were inspected but were less directly aligned because their main geometry concerns graph interference or partial identification.
